slides.title: What Are Arrays
slides.content: Arrays store multiple values of the same type in a single variable. They have a fixed size once created.

slides.title: Declaring Arrays
slides.content: Use square brackets to declare an array type. The `new` keyword creates the array in memory.

slides.title: Accessing Elements
slides.content: Array elements are accessed by index in square brackets. Indices start at 0.

slides.title: Array.Length
slides.content: The Length property returns the total number of elements. It is useful for loops and bounds checking.

exercise.prompt: What does `array.Length` return for a 3-element array?

slides.title: Foreach with Arrays
slides.content: Foreach simplifies iteration when you only need the value, not the index. It is read-only for the element.

slides.title: Multidimensional Arrays
slides.content: Use commas in brackets for multidimensional arrays. Access elements with multiple indices.

exercise.prompt: A 2D array uses _____ brackets with a comma

slides.title: Common Array Methods
slides.content: The Array class provides useful methods like Sort, Reverse, and IndexOf for common operations.

exercise.prompt: Which method sorts an array in place?

slides.title: Best Practices
slides.content: Always check bounds before accessing. Use foreach for simple reading. Prefer List<T> for dynamic sizes.

exercise.prompt: Create an array with 3 integers and print each using foreach
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: foreach, Console.WriteLine
When run, your code should output: 10, 20, 30

slides.title: Flow Builder: Arrays and Foreach
slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to declare an array and loop through it with foreach.
